In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
concomitant allergen/endotoxin exposure may be an important risk factor for the development of asthma.
concomitant allergen-endotoxin exposure may result in a synergistic inflammatory response in the airways of atopic asthematics.
exposure to both allergen (and other aeroallergen) and endotoxin in atopic asthmatics may be an important factor in the pathogenesis of asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

atopic asthmatic individuals have an exaggerated airway inflammatory response to concomitantly administered allergen and endotxin, which may contribute to the increased severity and frequency of asthmatic exacerbations.
the concomitant exposure of atopic asthma patients to endotoxin and antigen results in a synergistic response.
concomitant allergen/endotoxin exposure results in greater airway responses than exposure to either stimulus alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the airway response to allergen and/or endotoxin is influenced by a complex interplay between genetic and environmental factors.
the combination of allergen and endotxoin exposure results in greater airway inflammation than exposure to allergen or endotoxin alone.
the combination of endotoxin and antigen exposure may be more important in the development of allergic asthma than either stimulus alone.
